slides.headline: He was executed at 19 for plotting an armed uprising against British rule. Bhagat Singh later carried his photo.
Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged at Lahore Central Jail on November 16, 1915, at age 19.
slides.body: A Ghadar Party revolutionary, Sarabha was arrested in March 1915 and convicted in the First Lahore Conspiracy Case for plotting an armed uprising against British colonial rule in Punjab.

slides.headline: His conviction didn't end his influence - it spread it.
slides.body: Bhagat Singh, then a teenager, is said to have carried Sarabha's photograph and considered him a personal hero, carrying his example forward into the next generation of India's independence movement.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat still draws on the example of people who gave everything at an age most are just getting started.
slides.body: Sarabha didn't live to see independence - but the movement he died for outlived him by over three decades, carried forward by the people he inspired.

sources.text: Scroll.in - The 1915 Ghadar plan to free India from the British was a failure - but it sparked a revolution
